summary:
I re-authored cmcr-1653405 to version 1.1.0, replacing the 1.0.0 template. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClinicalCraft/61c17a21-a923-5d20-a08c-1c8a508459b0/scratchpad/pr5/wt/packages/content/cases/cmcr-1653405/case.json and README.md. The builder is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClinicalCraft/61c17a21-a923-5d20-a08c-1c8a508459b0/scratchpad/work-cmcr-1653405/: build.py, build_part1-3.py, score.ts, NOTES.md.

WHAT IT TEACHES. A 69-year-old woman (pseudonym 严淑芳 / Yan Shufang) is admitted with a month of recurrent abdominal distension and nausea. She has a hard, irregular, tender liver and multiple liver masses. The case teaches five things:
- Work up liver masses safely and characterise them before taking tissue.
- Read tumour markers and FDG-PET/CT within their limits.
- Plan a liver-lesion biopsy as a high-bleeding-risk procedure.
- Manage multifocal hepatic angiosarcoma: sarcoma team, systemic therapy or best supportive care, no transplant or curative resection.
- Prepare for tumour haemorrhage, and discuss a death that follows a biopsy without asserting a cause.

PHASES (static clock, 4):
1. admission: history, examination, ultrasound and tumour markers.
2. imaging: opens on decision 1; holds the PET/CT result dated "before the biopsy".
3. diagnosis: opens on decision 3 plus the biopsy act; holds the histology record.
4. outcome: opens only when all five decisions are made; learnerSwitchable false. It holds the death record and the two approved figures, and the patient does not speak in it.

DECISIONS (5, each with 4–5 options named by content, every option with its own feedback that names its guidance):
1. next-step, key characterise-and-stage: multiphase CT or MRI, blood count, clotting and liver tests before planning a biopsy.
2. pet-reading, key malignant-bleeding-untyped: probably a malignant tumour with bleeding inside it, but PET cannot type it.
3. tissue-plan, key planned-core-biopsy: image-guided core biopsy through normal liver, after platelets, clotting and antithrombotics are checked, with blood grouped and observation afterwards.
4. after-histology, key sarcoma-team-plan: immunostains on the existing core, sarcoma team, systemic therapy or best supportive care.
5. bleed-plan, key escalation-plan: observation, blood available, embolisation ready, mechanical VTE prophylaxis, limits of treatment discussed with her.

INTERVENTIONS (12):
- The report's own act: core-biopsy.
- Today's steps: hpb-mdt, ir-bleed-plan, post-biopsy-obs, mechanical-vte, oncology-referral, palliative-referral, goals-of-care.
- Tempting wrong steps, each with a harm text naming its guidance: repeat-biopsy, lmwh-prophylaxis, blind-ffp, transplant-referral.
- critical: true (risk high): core-biopsy when given on admission or before the blood count and clotting are ordered, and repeat-biopsy at any time.
- critical: false (moderate): lmwh-prophylaxis and blind-ffp.
- Indicated windows exclude anything done after the outcome has been read, so there is no hindsight credit.

RUBRIC: 13 deterministic items (weight 33) plus one examiner-judged communication item (Calgary–Cambridge, SPIKES, consent for the biopsy, teach-back). Two critical items, both acts:
- rb-safe-biopsy: {intervened: core-biopsy, whenIndicated: true}.
- rb-no-harm: the avoided harms; its scoredWhen lists every harmful act and the decisions that expose them.

STAFF: hepatology attending (Socratic, PEARLS, never reveals the diagnosis), ward nurse (ISBAR), radiologist, pathologist, interventional radiologist. History has 22 items (8 required, 17 unknown and said in her own voice). Investigations: 13; the 8 tests the report does not report say "No result is recorded for this test." There are 51 test utterances. The debrief has 6 dated, guideline-attributed teaching points.

MEASURED SCORES (core assess, 2026-11-14):
- Reference path: 33/33.
- Doing nothing: 0/30.
- Wrong first answer at all five decisions: 18/33 (55 %); at any single decision: 30/33.
- Biopsy on admission, or before the bloods are sent: 26/33, safety outcome FAIL.
- Repeat biopsy: 30/33, safety outcome FAIL.
- Enoxaparin, plasma or transplant referral: 30/33, rb-no-harm missed, safety outcome passes.
- Bleeding plan made only after reading the outcome: no credit (31/33).
extraction:
Every 1.0.0 fact (commit 88ed0d2, case.json and README) and where it is in 1.1.0:
- 69 years, female → patient.
- Abdominal distension and nausea for 1 month (腹胀伴恶心 1 个月) → chiefComplaint, openingLine; history bloating and duration.
- Recurrent (title; 反复腹胀; "这一阵反复出现 / It has been recurring") → history pattern; title kept.
- No fever, no jaundice (皮肤发黄), no abdominal pain → history fever, jaundice, pain.
- No history of malignancy → history cancer-history.
- Liver edge about 5 cm below the xiphoid, from the admission examination (hepatomegaly in the triage note) → exam liver-edge, admission phase.
- Liver hard, surface not smooth, tender → exam liver-texture.
- CA125 38.10 U/mL and CA19-9 68.60 U/mL raised; CEA, AFP, CA15-3 and CA72-4 reported normal → investigation markers, admission phase, with values: no reference ranges added, flagged H/N.
- Multiple heterogeneous solid liver masses, largest about 12.0×10.5 cm, 考虑恶性 / suspicious for malignancy → abd-us, admission phase.
- 18F-FDG PET/CT: multiple heterogeneous FDG-avid lesions, SUVmax 7.1, largest about 11.2×10.6×7.9 cm with low central uptake, read as malignancy with intratumoural haemorrhage and intrahepatic spread → pet-ct, imaging and diagnosis phases.
- PET/CT suggested haemorrhage before the biopsy (1.0.0 decision feedback) → pet-ct dated "before the biopsy"; keyReasoning 6; teaching point 5.
- Right-lobe mass biopsy (肝右叶肿物穿刺): angiosarcoma; individual immunostains not given → histology record (diagnosis and outcome phases); ihc has no result.
- Death from intrahepatic haemorrhage a few days later; no resuscitation detail; no proof the biopsy caused it → outcome record.
- Source title "primary multiple hepatic angiosarcoma, 18F-FDG PET/CT" → citation, conclusion.
- Setting inpatient → setting and facility.
- 1.0.0 unknowns (immunostains, coagulation, haemodynamics, resuscitation records) → unknowns and debrief.unknowns.
- Figures fig01 (ultrasound) and fig03 (histology) approved; fig02 and the PDF withheld → assets fig01 and fig03, attached to the outcome record only.

Contradictions and differences kept in neutral wording and listed under README "To verify":
(a) The PET/CT conclusion: the zh text has 肿瘤内出血及肝内转移 with no "malignant"; the en text has "malignancy… intrahepatic spread". 1.1.0 states both readings.
(b) "A few days later" has no stated starting day.
(c) The history records no abdominal pain while the examination records a tender liver; both are kept.
(d) The timing of the ultrasound and markers relative to the PET/CT and to the admission is not recorded (staging choice, labelled).
(e) When the histology was reported relative to the haemorrhage is not recorded (labelled teaching device).

Inferences (derived, not new):
- 12 cm is the rounded first dimension of the largest mass.
- 7.2 ± 2.6 months is quoted as "about 7 months" (ELTR guidance figure, not a patient fact).
- The haemorrhage is taught as "within the tumour". The case does not assert which lesion bled, although 1.0.0's sentence attaches it to the cold centre of the largest lesion.
- 穿刺 is rendered as "needle biopsy"; core versus aspirate is not recorded.
- "Multifocal" is taken from "multiple".

Stays unknown: vital signs; blood count and platelets; PT/INR, APTT and fibrinogen; liver and renal function; hepatitis serology; cirrhosis; ascites and spleen; medicines including antithrombotics; allergies; alcohol and smoking; occupational exposures (vinyl chloride, arsenic, thorium dioxide, radiation); weight; family history; performance status; how the biopsy was done and how she was prepared and observed; any multiphase CT or MRI; extrahepatic disease; immunohistochemistry; the course of the haemorrhage, any transfusion, embolisation or surgery, and autopsy; what she was told and what she wished.

Teaching devices (labelled in the README; they add no clinical fact):
- The staging into four phases.
- The tests a clinician would order today, with no recorded results.
- The learner planning and performing the biopsy (the report records that it was done, not how).
- The patient's voiced worry ("something serious").
- Her knowledge that a sample was taken, staged for the SPIKES conversation.
- The staff, decisions, interventions and scoring.

The pseudonym changed to 严淑芳 / Yan Shufang (unique in the library).
safetyFixes: 1.0.0's only critical item was a causality quiz scored on a first attempt and answerable in hindsight. It is replaced by two critical acts: rb-safe-biopsy ({intervened: core-biopsy, whenIndicated: true}, i.e. the biopsy after the further imaging and after the blood count and clotting were ordered) and rb-no-harm (the avoided harms, with a full scoredWhen).

core-biopsy is critical: true (risk high). It is contraindicated on admission (before cross-sectional imaging) and whenever the blood count or clotting has not been ordered. The keyed decision, its feedback and the reference path all name the preconditions (platelets, INR and antithrombotics; image guidance through normal liver; blood grouped; observation for at least 3 hours; interventional radiology ready).
repeat-biopsy is critical: true: no second pass into a vascular, already-haemorrhagic tumour just to obtain immunostains, which are done on the existing block.

Drug VTE prophylaxis (lmwh-prophylaxis, critical false) is contraindicated throughout and mechanical prophylaxis is keyed (NICE NG89: balance bleeding risk; BSG 2020: prophylactic LMWH stopped 12 h before a biopsy).
Blind plasma (blind-ffp, critical false) is contraindicated: BSG 2020 says no FFP to correct an INR of 2.0 or below, and SIR 2019 corrects only a measured INR.
A transplant referral is contraindicated once the histology is known (ELTR 2013: absolute contraindication), and resection is a distractor for multifocal disease.

Acts scored in time (the interventional-radiology bleeding plan, post-biopsy observation, oncology referral, goals of care, mechanical prophylaxis) have indicatedWhen windows that exclude anything done after the outcome record has been read. It was measured: making the plan after reading the outcome earns nothing.

Removed every spoiler visible before the histology (a distractor and feedback naming a sarcoma; a referral named 'sarcoma team' that is visible from the start) and authoring language in the patient's voice (1.0.0's 'the source notes do not provide that information' answers).
guidelines: ACG (American College of Gastroenterology), Clinical Guideline: Focal Liver Lesions, 2024 (Frenette et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2024;119(7):1235-1271). Checked online: full text read for rec. 1 (multiphasic CT/MRI), rec. 8 (ruptured adenoma: stabilisation then embolisation and/or resection), rec. 26, key concept 40 and the angiosarcoma text.

BSG/RCR/RCPath, Guidelines on the use of liver biopsy in clinical practice, 2020 (Neuberger et al., Gut 2020;69(8):1382-1403). Checked online: full text on PMC for image guidance of focal lesions, INR <2.0 for a lesional biopsy, no FFP at INR ≤2.0, platelets <50 → transvenous approach where possible, observation ≥3 h, no day case when malignancy is strongly suspected, LMWH stop times.

SIR (Society of Interventional Radiology), Consensus guidelines for periprocedural management of thrombotic and bleeding risk, Part II: Recommendations, 2019 (Patel IJ et al., J Vasc Interv Radiol 2019;30(8):1168-1184.e1). Checked online: citation verified; thresholds taken from a published summary (solid organ biopsy = high risk; INR ≤1.5–1.8; platelets transfused below 50×10^9/L), because the full text was not accessible.

National Health Commission of China (国家卫生健康委), 原发性肝癌诊疗指南（2024年版）, 2024 (协和医学杂志 2024;15(3):532-558). Checked online: official PDF read for the biopsy section (platelets and clotting first, 18G/16G cores, a route through normal liver, repeat biopsy only when the sample is inadequate or the result is discordant) and for AFP-negative disease.

ESMO–EURACAN–GENTURIS, Soft tissue and visceral sarcomas Clinical Practice Guidelines, 2021 (Gronchi et al., Ann Oncol 2021;32(11):1348-1365). Checked online: preprint full text read for multiple ≥14–16G cores after imaging and MDT, PET/CT as a problem-solving tool [IV, A], anthracycline first line [I, A], taxanes in angiosarcoma [III, B].
NICE NG89, Venous thromboembolism in over 16s, 2018 (updated 2019). Checked online: PDF read for recs 1.1.3, 1.1.8, 1.4.6, 1.3.16 and 1.7.1.

European Liver Transplant Registry (Orlando et al.), Hepatic hemangiosarcoma: an absolute contraindication to liver transplantation, Transplantation 2013;95(6):872-877. Checked online (Europe PMC abstract): mean survival 7.2 months, none beyond 23 months.
Kang et al., Safety of percutaneous biopsy for hepatic angiosarcoma, J Vasc Interv Radiol 2016;27(6):846-851. Checked online (abstract): severe bleeding in 3 of 33, no biopsy-related deaths.
Baile et al., SPIKES protocol for delivering bad news, Oncologist 2000;5(4):302-311. Not checked online: standard citation.

Source pass: the order and setting of the ultrasound and tumour markers relative to the PET/CT and the admission; whether a multiphase CT or MRI was done.
Source pass: the values and reference ranges for CEA, AFP, CA15-3 and CA72-4.
Source pass: biopsy route, guidance and needle (core or aspirate), number of passes, any tract plugging, the pre-biopsy platelets and INR, post-biopsy observation, and the immunohistochemistry panel.
Source pass: what 'a few days later' counts from; when and how the haemorrhage presented; any transfusion, embolisation or surgery; autopsy; when the histology was reported relative to the bleeding.

Source pass: history the template dropped (vital signs, medicines and antithrombotics, alcohol, hepatitis or cirrhosis, exposures, performance status) and examination findings (ascites, spleen); confirm the tender liver alongside no abdominal pain.
Source pass: the content of fig01 and fig03, to decide whether fig01 can be shown with the admission ultrasound result instead of only in the outcome phase.
Clinician (hepatology, interventional radiology, sarcoma oncology): the five keyed answers, especially multiphase CT or MRI before biopsy and the escalation plan in decision 5.

Clinician: the critical flags (premature or unprepared biopsy and repeat biopsy as safety failures; enoxaparin and plasma as non-critical), and contraindicating drug VTE prophylaxis from admission onward rather than from the PET/CT onward.
Clinician: applying the 2024 Chinese HCC guideline's biopsy section to a liver lesion of unknown type, and ACG 2024's ruptured-adenoma recommendation by analogy to tumour bleeding.
Citation pass: the SIR 2019 Part II thresholds were confirmed only through a published summary, because the full text was not accessible.
